when: after 8:00, a dragon is up and grubs have not been taken
asks: they're on dragon, what do we take

say: Give it and start grubs the moment they show on dragon, or take top plates if your jungler can't get there in time.
more: A trade only works if it starts when theirs starts. Wait until the dragon is dead and they are already walking up to stop you.
Grubs do not come back, so getting them for one early dragon is a fair price. The payoff shows up later, when you start hitting towers.
If your jungler is too far away, plates are the fallback: gold now, and a tower that falls sooner.
check: How many enemies are showing at the dragon, and is your jungler on the top side?
breaks: Wrong if this dragon puts them on soul point: then group and contest it instead of trading.

they took the grubs, do we do dragon
grubs are gone, what do we take
they're all top, what do I do bot
say: Go straight to dragon while they're still walking back from the top pit, or take bot plates if your jungler's low.
more: They just spent their jungler and probably two laners on the top side. The dragon is as far from them as anything on the map.
Grubs help them break towers later. A dragon back keeps you level in the race toward soul, which matters more as the game goes on.
Plates are the answer when nobody can Smite: you still get paid for the time they spent up there.
check: Is your jungler healthy with Smite up, and did their bot lane stay in lane?

say: Take the one on the side where your lanes are pushed and let them have the other, or go for both only if their jungler's dead.
more: The pit you can reach with more players is the one you win. A straight swap of Herald for dragon is a normal, even result.
Herald pays in tower gold and opens the map soon. Dragon pays later, as the stacks add up toward soul.
Splitting your team to grab both usually loses both, unless they have no Smite to answer with.
check: Which of your side lanes is pushed in, and is Herald actually alive?
breaks: Wrong if they already have two or three dragons: then the dragon side matters more, so move your strong lane there first.

tower or drake
should we trade tower for dragon
do I hit tower or go to dragon
say: An outer tower for an early dragon is a fair swap, so take it fast, or go contest if you'd arrive together with waves pushed.
more: A tower is gold for everyone near it and it opens their jungle on that side. One early dragon is a small bonus by itself.
The swap goes bad if you only get half a tower. Commit fully so it falls before they walk back.
Later, with that tower gone, their side of the map is darker and harder for them to defend.
check: How much health does the tower have, and how many of you are there to hit it?

Starting Baron makes them choose. If they turn to stop you, the dragon stays alive and you fight on your terms.
Plan your recall about a minute before it spawns, so you arrive with items and full health.

breaks: Wrong if Baron is slow for your team and they simply finish the dragon: then drop Baron early and go contest as five.

more: Baron turns into towers and inhibitors over the next few minutes. A single dragon that isn't soul doesn't stop that push.

If they get it, your job is to give them no fight: stay behind towers and kill minions from range.

more: A couple of camps is a small amount of gold for one player. A dragon is a buff for five.

say: Keep hitting and take the tower or inhibitor if your team can stall under their own tower, or Teleport in if the fight decides Baron.
more: If they send nobody, they're paying for the fight with buildings. Make that as expensive as possible.
Your team's job is to not fight. Backing up under a tower while you push is a win.
If a game-deciding objective is on the line, your body there matters more than one more tower.
check: Can your team disengage, and is Baron, soul or elder at stake?
breaks: Wrong if your team is already dying: then stop and get back to defend your base.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

should I split as adc
is it safe to get that wave
can I push bot alone
say: Catch the wave on your side of the river and come back, or go further only with a teammate when four enemies show.
more: You need the gold, but a carry caught alone is the easiest way for them to start an objective.
Waves that have crossed to your half are nearly free. Past the river, they're bait.
Let a tougher teammate take the long lane. You take mid and the nearby wave.

breaks: Wrong if an objective spawns within a minute: then skip the wave and stay with your team.

I can't fight, where do I go
I'm losing, side lane or group
how do I catch up
say: Catch side waves near your towers for gold without fighting anyone, or group if your team needs your crowd control more than your damage.
more: Minions and towers give you gold without having to beat anyone. That's how a behind player gets back.
Don't push past the river. You lose the duel if someone comes.
A tank or support-style champion can be useful in fights even when behind, so being there may matter more.
check: Where are the side waves, and who could come to your lane?
breaks: Wrong if their split pusher is in the same lane and stronger than you: then swap lanes with a teammate who can hold him.

asks: my team just died, do I keep pushing
they wiped, finish tower?
team's dead, do I go back
I'm splitting and we lost the fight
say: Stop pushing and get back to defend, or finish the tower only if it's nearly dead and you couldn't reach base in time anyway.
more: With your team dead, the enemy is free to turn on you or on your base. Both are bad places to be alone.
Clearing waves at your base until respawns is what keeps the game alive.
One tower is a fair consolation if you truly can't get home in time.
check: How long are the respawn timers, and where are the enemies heading?
breaks: Wrong if their base is open and you can win a race to the nexus with a big wave: check that before you leave.

asks: we got baron, where do I go
baron buff, split or group
how do we use baron
what lane do I push with baron
say: Recall, buy, then push a side lane with the main group mid, or group as five if you can't duel whoever comes.
more: Baron makes minions hard to clear. Pressure in more than one lane is what breaks a base.
Buy first. A lead sitting in your inventory as gold doesn't hit towers any harder.
The side laner's job is to make someone come. If two come, the group mid takes the tower.
check: How much gold are you holding, and who on their team clears waves best?
breaks: Wrong if their team has strong engage and you're the carry: then stay with the group and let a tougher teammate take the side.

what do I do before baron
do I push side first
should we just go start baron
say: Get both side waves moving first and then meet at Baron, or leave one strong duelist in the side lane to pull someone away.
more: Waves pushing into their base force a choice: clear them or come to the pit. They can't do both with five.
If they answer the waves, you start Baron with more players. If they don't, the waves take towers.
The same push can end at the dragon instead, if that's the better target.
check: Where are the three waves, and how many enemies are showing?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler is alive and unseen while you start it short-handed: then use Baron as a threat and fight whoever walks in.

when do I stop pushing
soul dragon soon, stay side?

say: Shove one last wave and walk to your team now, or stay only if Teleport's up and you'll use it before the fight starts.
more: This is the fight the game turns on. A tower doesn't make up for losing it.
The wave you push first keeps working while you walk, so you lose nothing by leaving.
Teleport lets you stay longer, but only if you press it early.

say: Ward the jungle between your splitter and their team so he sees who's coming, or stay with your carry if he's alone mid.
more: A split push lives on information. One ward on the path to his lane is what lets him stay.
Your carry still needs you. Don't leave him alone to place it if their engage is nearby.
Deep wards also tell your group when it's safe to start an objective.

say: Farm the camps beside your split pusher so you can turn on whoever answers him, or sit on the opposite side and threaten the objective.
more: Near him, a two-player answer from them becomes an even fight they didn't plan for.
On the far side, you make them choose between stopping him and stopping you.
Pick based on what's up: if an objective is alive, be next to that.

say: Take the side wave when it's past the middle and be back before the next mid wave, or stay if nobody else can hold mid.
more: Mid is the lane that guards both rivers. Leaving it empty costs more than the side wave pays.
A quick shove and return gets you both waves.
If a teammate with good wave clear is mid, you're free to stay out longer.
